question: After the stale-policy defect is fixed, should deny-over-allow be a permanent exec security contract across both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json, including forced human prompts in full/off mode?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes the execution security boundary and adds two operator policy surfaces, so implementation review cannot choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Accept both policy layers
options.body: Land after locked and pre-dispatch denylist revalidation is complete, preserving the documented union semantics.

options.title: Narrow to approvals file
options.body: Keep denylist only in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface before merge.

options.title: Decline the feature
options.body: Keep existing full/off semantics and close the denylist implementation attempts.

recommendation.title: Accept both policy layers
recommendation.body: Land after locked and pre-dispatch denylist revalidation is complete, preserving the documented union semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work defines the authorization and policy-revalidation contract affected by this choice.
